summary: Platform-specific binary is a WebRTC-signaled remote shell (PTY + /bin/bash driven by network peer)
details: This linux-arm64 companion package ships `bin/sxt`, a Go ELF that combines a PTY (`github.com/creack/pty`, `/dev/ptmx`, `pty.StartWithSize`) spawning `/bin/bash` / `/bin/sh` / `/bin/zsh` with a full Pion WebRTC stack (`pion/webrtc/v4`, `pion/ice`, `pion/dtls`, `pion/sctp`, `pion/turn`, `pion/stun`), `coder/websocket` signaling, and `skip2/go-qrcode` pairing. Bytes received on a WebRTC `OnDataChannel` are written into the local shell PTY, giving whoever holds the pairing token/QR full interactive command execution on the host. Provenance strengthens the malicious reading: although the package is published as `sextant-cli-linux-arm64`, its manifest points at `https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control` — a handle referencing DDoS and a repo named after remote control of Claude — inconsistent with a legitimate vendor-owned platform companion. The sub-package itself declares no `scripts`, `main`, or `bin`, so `npm install` of this artifact alone runs no code; the backdoor executes when the parent CLI package (or the user) invokes `sxt`, at which point the shipped binary opens the host to remote shell access over WebRTC.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
